briefing: The window was lighter on sized capital-flow news than recent runs, but added fresh evidence on three fronts: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told IMF and World Bank policymakers that an internal scenario puts potential 2030 US GDP as high as $44 trillion under an extreme AI-adoption case, a bullish framing delivered just as his company prepares a possible $2 trillion IPO. On the friction side, major US banks including Schwab and JPMorgan confirmed they are actively blocking outside AI agents such as Meta's Muse from moving client money, and the OpenCode developer platform disclosed a breach tied to a large-scale model-distillation attack that exposed OpenAI and Anthropic API keys for 1.4% of its users. Commercially, NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops reached retail and DeepSeek shipped another free open-weight model update, both signs that compute and model competition continue regardless of financing-market jitters.

roi_analysis.verdict: Lab-side rhetoric about AI's economic upside is accelerating ahead of Anthropic's IPO, but concrete enterprise behavior this window points the other way: major financial institutions are restricting rather than embracing autonomous AI agents over liability concerns, and a new AI-platform security breach adds to the operational costs of deploying agentic AI at scale.
supporting_points: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the IMF and World Bank's annual meetings that an internal economic model projects AI could expand US GDP to roughly $44 trillion by 2030, about 30% above a no-AI baseline, under an extreme adoption scenario (Reuters via Yahoo Finance).

NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops, a commercial local-AI product, went on sale this window from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo and Microsoft, showing continued retail-level monetization of AI hardware investment beyond data-center GPU sales (NVIDIA).
DeepSeek's free, rapid-fire open-weight model updates (V4.1-Flash-1017) continue to lower the cost of frontier-adjacent AI capability for downstream enterprise adopters (Bloomberg).
counter_points: Charles Schwab and JPMorgan both confirmed they are actively blocking unauthorized third-party AI agents, including Meta's Muse, from moving client money, citing unresolved liability questions — a concrete sign that large regulated enterprises are curbing rather than expanding agentic AI autonomy (Forkast, citing Bloomberg Television).

OpenCode disclosed a security breach tied to a large-scale model-distillation attack that exposed OpenAI and Anthropic API keys for 1.4% of its Console users, adding to the operational and trust costs enterprises must weigh when adopting agentic AI tooling (CyberSecurityNews).

Clark's own $44 trillion figure is explicitly framed as an extreme, non-forecast scenario, and he paired it with a call for 'unusual and serious' international rules, undercutting the certainty of the bullish framing even as it was delivered ahead of Anthropic's prospective $2 trillion IPO (Reuters).

by_layer.infrastructure: No new infrastructure-financing disclosures arrived in this window; NVIDIA's RTX Spark retail shipment is a modest positive data point at the device layer, while CoreWeave and Oracle balance-sheet stress flagged in prior runs remains unaddressed.
by_layer.labs: Anthropic is actively pitching an optimistic, policy-maker-facing growth narrative ahead of its IPO, a rhetorical escalation that sits alongside its previously disclosed cash-flow-positive Q3 but does not add new financial evidence this window.
by_layer.enterprise: The clearest enterprise-layer signal this window is defensive: regulated financial institutions are restricting AI-agent autonomy over liability risk, and a platform-level security breach shows real operational costs from agentic AI adoption, both cutting against a simple 'AI pays for itself' narrative.

roi_analysis.what_changed: No material change in stance from the prior run; this window sharpens the split between lab-level optimism about AI's economic ceiling and enterprise-level caution about deploying autonomous agents, without new sized capital flows or balance-sheet disclosures.

items.headline: Anthropic's Jack Clark tells IMF AI could push US GDP to $44 trillion
items.summary: Speaking at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said an internal company model forecasts that, under an extreme AI-adoption scenario, US economic output could reach roughly $44 trillion by 2030, and called for international 'unusual and serious rules' on the technology.
items.why_it_matters: A leading lab is now making an explicit macroeconomic case for AI's return on investment to policymakers just weeks ahead of its own prospective $2 trillion IPO, directly bearing on the standing question of whether AI spending will pay off.
items.confidence_note: The $44 trillion figure is explicitly framed by Anthropic itself as an extreme, non-forecast scenario rather than a prediction.

items.headline: Schwab, JPMorgan confirm they block outside AI agents from moving money
items.summary: Charles Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said the firm blocks 'tens and twenties' of unauthorized AI-agent attempts weekly, including Meta's Muse, from moving client funds, while JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon confirmed his bank is also blocking outside agents from accessing customer account information.
items.why_it_matters: Large regulated enterprises actively restricting rather than adopting autonomous AI agents over liability concerns is direct evidence against assumptions of rapid, unconstrained enterprise AI monetization.

items.headline: OpenCode breach exposes OpenAI, Anthropic API keys for 1.4% of users
items.summary: AI coding platform OpenCode disclosed a security breach tied to a large-scale distillation attack that exposed third-party API keys, including OpenAI and Anthropic credentials, for 1.4% of its Console users, and said it is working with the labs to remediate.
items.why_it_matters: A platform-level breach tied to unauthorized model distillation shows a concrete operational and trust cost of the agentic-AI tooling ecosystem that enterprises must weigh against AI's promised productivity gains.
items.confidence_note: Full technical details of the breach have not been disclosed by OpenCode, and the incident was still ongoing at time of reporting.

items.headline: NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops go on sale from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft
items.summary: NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops, combining Blackwell RTX graphics with up to 128GB of unified memory and the full NVIDIA AI software stack, became available starting at $2,399 from major PC makers, bringing data-center-class local AI inference to premium Windows laptops.
items.why_it_matters: A mainstream retail launch of local-AI-capable hardware is a concrete product shipment translating NVIDIA's platform investment into consumer revenue, a data point for whether AI capex reaches real end-market demand.

items.headline: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017 update, opens Search and Fetch APIs
items.summary: DeepSeek released an updated open-weight model, V4.1-Flash-1017, claiming stronger benchmark performance and faster, shorter outputs than its predecessor at unchanged API pricing, while opening its Search and Fetch APIs to all developers.
items.why_it_matters: Continued rapid, free model upgrades from a low-cost Chinese lab keep pressuring the pricing power of frontier labs that enterprises are weighing for long-term AI spending commitments.
items.confidence_note: Benchmark claims are self-reported by DeepSeek and not yet independently verified by third-party evaluators.
